reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes an ETH MEV bot by claiming unusually large returns, including 100 ETH daily or every few hours, through following a tutorial and deploying the activity oneself. Wallet-style displays, a claimed increase to 10 ETH in two days, and a 10/10 endorsement are presented as support for the opportunity. The website's ownership, the authenticity or source of the displayed transactions, and whether viewers had to pay, transfer assets, or provide information remain unverified.

citations.quote: Make 100 ETH Every Single Day with MEV BOT
You want to make over 100 ETH every couple of hours?
Here on the website, mvblogguide.com, right here you can read the tutorial and learn how to do it yourself.
Here you can see the intervals of payments he's receiving into his wallet.

opening.argument: The strongest responsible reading is that this is an unverified demonstration, not a promise that viewers will receive the same result. The material presents a claimed example and points viewers toward information, but it does not establish that the displayed transactions came from the bot, that the result is repeatable, or that any viewer is guaranteed a return. The headline is attention-grabbing, yet the underlying evidence remains a claim requiring independent research rather than proof of deception. The video also does not establish that viewers were asked to deposit funds, surrender credentials, or pay a fee. On this record, uncertainty about authenticity is a reason for caution, not sufficient evidence that the content is a scam.

citations.quote: Make 100 ETH Every Single Day with MEV BOT
Here you can see the intervals of payments he's receiving into his wallet.
It contains all the information that you need.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats large claims as proof of deception, but the quotes establish only what the speaker said and showed. A wallet-style display does not by itself establish its origin or falsity, and the prosecution expressly concedes that payment, transfer, and information requests are unverified. The tutorial reference can equally support an informational presentation whose claims require checking, rather than a proven scam mechanism.

citations.quote: You want to make over 100 ETH every couple of hours?
Here on the website, mvblogguide.com, right here you can read the tutorial and learn how to do it yourself.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing proof of a deposit request does not neutralize the affirmative promotion. The video pairs an extraordinary earnings claim with wallet-payment imagery, a personal profit claim, and a favorable rating. Calling the claims unverified does not make them cautious; it leaves the central financial representation unsupported. The displayed wallet activity still does not show that the bot caused the returns or that viewers could reproduce them.

citations.quote: I started 2 days ago with 3.5 ETH and now I'm at 10 ETH,
I rate this bot a 10 out of 10.

opening.argument: The content can be classified by its operational subject: it directs attention to an MEV-bot tutorial and explains where to read instructions and how to carry out the process. That is consistent with a technology demonstration or educational walkthrough. Showing an interface, describing payment intervals, and reporting a personal experience are not the same as proving that the creator is operating a fraudulent scheme. The record does not establish that the tutorial requires a fee, that the speaker controls the linked site, or that the claimed result is presented as a legally enforceable guarantee. Even a positive review can be mistaken or overenthusiastic without being scam content.

citations.quote: Here on the website, mvblogguide.com, right here you can read the tutorial and learn how to do it yourself.
I started 2 days ago with 3.5 ETH and now I'm at 10 ETH,

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's characterization assumes that instructional context is merely a delivery vehicle for fraud. But its own evidence describes a tutorial and a personal account, not a request for money or credentials. The transaction display may illustrate the speaker's explanation, while the supplied record does not authenticate it or show that anyone was induced to transfer assets. The content's subject therefore remains a tool and its claimed operation.

citations.quote: It contains all the information that you need.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Instructional packaging is precisely what can make a financial promotion persuasive; it does not convert extraordinary earnings claims into neutral education. The presentation tells viewers to learn how to do it themselves, cites wallet payments, reports more than seven ETH in profit, and assigns a 10/10 rating. None of those elements establishes that the tutorial works, that the returns are genuine, or that the bot caused them.

citations.quote: Here on the website, mvblogguide.com, right here you can read the tutorial and learn how to do it yourself.
Nesting a profit of over 7 ETH.
I rate this bot a 10 out of 10.

opening.argument: At most, the material promotes access to an external technology service or tutorial. The supplied evidence does not show a deposit instruction, a required purchase, a fee, a referral hierarchy, a request for credentials, or a promise that viewers will recover money. It also does not establish who owns the website or whether the displayed transactions are authentic. Those omissions matter: a high-risk or exaggerated product presentation may be poor commerce, but the scam mechanism cannot be inferred solely from an earnings claim. The safer classification is ordinary promotion of a purported tool whose safety and performance remain for the viewer to evaluate.

citations.quote: Mev bot Tutorial - https://mevbotguide.com/
Here on the website, mvblogguide.com, right here you can read the tutorial and learn how to do it yourself.
It contains all the information that you need.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies no demonstrated transaction between the creator and a viewer. It acknowledges that whether viewers had to pay, transfer assets, or provide information remains unverified. The presence of a website and a claimed return therefore supports, at most, promotion of a purported service; it does not establish the missing mechanism that would distinguish a scam from an ordinary, possibly unreliable commercial offering.

citations.quote: Mev bot Tutorial - https://mevbotguide.com/
It contains all the information that you need.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A scam classification need not wait for a visible credential request or completed victim transfer when the content promotes a purported trading tool through implausible returns. Here the promotion is not ordinary retail marketing: it emphasizes over 100 ETH every few hours, wallet payments, rapid personal profit, and a perfect rating. The record's inability to verify the website or transactions is evidence that the promotional claims are unsupported, not evidence that they are ordinary and reliable.
